differential.name: Colorectal adenocarcinoma
differential.rationale: Age ≥ 65, positive fecal hemoglobin (425 ng/mL) and known colon polyp raise suspicion for malignant transformation.

differential.name: Advanced adenomatous polyp (large sessile or villous adenoma)
differential.rationale: Large or villous polyps can bleed occultly and are common precursors in this age group.

differential.name: Diverticular disease with lower GI bleeding
differential.rationale: Diverticulosis is prevalent in older adults and can cause intermittent occult bleeding.

differential.name: Colonic angiodysplasia
differential.rationale: Vascular ectasia of the colon often presents with painless occult bleeding in the elderly.

differential.name: NSAID‑induced colonic ulcer/erosion
differential.rationale: Medication review is pending; NSAID use can cause mucosal injury and occult blood loss.
